set.body:
Scheduling lane: maintenance. Current plan: docs/refactor/PLAN.md. Live dependency edges supersede historical sequencing below.

Current disposition, 2026-09-19; governing docs/refactor/PLAN.md.
Retained with its original acceptance scope; recheck against current code before implementation or closure. Not a prerequisite for the annotation-assisted preview.

Original scope retained below for evidence; fleet procedure/assignments are historical and do not govern single-developer work.

OWNER ASK: "take an ASCII text file of a story, run a CLI, get our annotated markup plus an HTML
preview that shows the markup graphically." MEASURED ANSWER: THE RENDERER EXISTS AND IS GOOD; THE
INPUT PATH DOES NOT EXIST.

WHAT WE HAVE, in storyatlas4s (NOT storymodel4s -- storymodel4s has NO cli module and emits no HTML
or SVG at all; I grepped every .scala for `<html`, `<svg`, `text/html` and found nothing):

  cli/.../Main.scala        `storyatlas4s edition --out <dir>`
  cli/.../Edition.scala     writes atlas .svg, codex .svg, codex-pages .html, receipt.json
  cli/.../CodexHtml.scala   the paginated Narrative Codex as ONE SELF-CONTAINED HTML DOCUMENT

CodexHtml is exactly the artifact the owner describes, and its contract is careful: each page is a
`.text` rail of one `<span class="line">` per TextFragment IN DOCUMENT ORDER with nothing between
them, so the concatenated span text IS the canonical text (V-T2); an inline SVG overlay lowered from
the same PaginatedCodex carries annotation piece ids as `data-name`, so A NAME RESOLVES THE SAME WAY
IN THE TEXT LAYER AND THE GRAPHIC LAYER (V-I2); no script, no external resource, and no colour
carries meaning. That is a visualization you can trust to be showing you the real structure.

WHAT IS MISSING IS THE INPUT. `Main` accepts only `--out <dir>`. Its one wired path is

    Edition.build(WarOfTheGhostsModel.model, "war-of-the-ghosts")

-- A HARDCODED FIXTURE. There is no `--in story.txt`.

AND THE REASON IS NOT LAZINESS, WHICH IS THE USEFUL PART. `Edition.build` is ALREADY GENERAL: it
takes `StoryModel[ModelStatus.Validated]`. So the CLI work is small. The gap is producing a validated
StoryModel FROM ARBITRARY ASCII PROSE, and that is Stage 1b -- bd-01M17MET0E4TWW304YKXPHBSBG, the
proposition provider, measured by grok at 4 OF 50 SENTENCES.

THIS IS THE SAME LONG POLE grok named against the chief's letter: "a real recall corpus arrives as
TEXT", and closing the compiler bead filled the severed NarrativeGraph link WITHOUT creating a method
that turns an arbitrary English sentence into a proposition. The owner's CLI ask and the corpus
requirement are BLOCKED ON THE SAME THING, which is worth knowing because it means one piece of work
buys both.

SCOPE OF THIS BEAD, in two parts that can land separately:
  PART A, executable the moment Stage 1b produces charts for a file: `storyatlas4s edition
    --in <story.txt> --out <dir>`, routed through the existing general `Edition.build`. Small.
  PART B, executable NOW and worth doing first: point the CLI at a SECOND fixture besides WOG, to
    prove `Edition.build`'s generality is real rather than assumed. If it only ever renders one
    model, "already general" is a claim nobody has tested.

Part B is the honest first slice and it needs no corpus, no REB, and no provider.
set.title: [maintenance] CLI: Unicode text to source and surface bundle now; semantic markup waits for Stage 1b
